clue.text: Like letter in Dombey and Son that a lot of people get

definitions.text: Like letter in Dombey and Son
definitions.meaning: first meaning: shaped like O, the letter that appears in both Dombey and Son

definitions.text: that a lot of people get
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a letter or notice sent round to many recipients

explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to a letter written in the Dickens novel; the first sense is the round letter O, which recurs in 'Dombey' and 'Son'.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter O is round in shape, and a notice distributed to many people is also called by this word.

clue.text: A couple of letters said to deliver final blow

indicators.note: said means the names of the letters are spoken, and the answer spells out how they sound

parts.note: the two letters K and O, the boxing abbreviation for a knockout

explanation.surface: Someone claims two letters can be enough to finish off an opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: KO is the boxing abbreviation for a knockout; spoken as letter names it sounds like 'kay-oh', and that spelling is itself a word.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb this informal boxing term means to knock an opponent out, the decisive punch that ends a fight.

clue.text: Outline of character, say, son inscribed on boat

indicators.note: inscribed on means written upon, so in this down clue the letter for son sits on top of the boat

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A boat's name painted on the hull reads like a brief description of somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'say' marks a character sketch as one example of the kind of brief outline meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A character sketch is a short descriptive piece giving the main features of a person, a rough outline rather than a full portrait.

clue.text: Recipients of letters I sorted wrongly

indicators.note: wrongly means the letters of I and sorted are put in a different, incorrect order

explanation.surface: A clerk confesses to misfiling the post meant for the newspaper's letters page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sorted' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; the signal is 'wrongly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspaper letters pages are addressed to the editor, so editors are the people who receive readers' correspondence.

clue.text: Section of literature replaced by one letter that links two of them

definitions.text: letter that links two of them

indicators.note: section of points to a run of letters inside the word literature, the TER in its middle
replaced by means that run is swapped out for a single different letter, here G

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A passage of writing is reduced to one character that joins two others together.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the middle TER of LITERATURE and put the 'one letter' G in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: In typography a ligature is a single character joining two letters, as in æ or the joined fi.

clue.text: Something warm that may be used to press a suit

definitions.text: Something warm that may be used to press a suit

parts.words: Something warm that may be used to press a suit
parts.note: it sounds like a hot iron for pressing clothes, but the suit is a courtship pressed by a heartfelt written message

explanation.walkthrough: 'Press a suit' suggests ironing a jacket; to press one's suit is to pursue a courtship, and a warm, affectionate letter helps do it.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic note to a sweetheart is warm in feeling and is a traditional means of wooing someone.

clue.text: Is uplifting part of Christian year, like parts of hymn and psalm

definitions.text: like parts of hymn and psalm

indicators.note: in a down clue uplifting means the word is turned upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: Lent is the season of the church calendar before Easter

explanation.surface: A season of the church calendar is said to raise the spirits, much like a hymn or psalm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uplifting' looks like praise of hymns but turns IS upwards to SI. The parts meant are letters: the N of hymn and the P of psalm are not pronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: The final N of hymn and the opening P of psalm are written but never pronounced, so these letters are mute.

clue.text: Letters from first eleven taken wrongly

definitions.text: Letters from first eleven taken wrongly

parts.words: Letters from first eleven taken wrongly
parts.note: the word is spelt entirely from letters among the first eleven of the alphabet, A to K, and means seized unlawfully

explanation.walkthrough: 'First eleven' suggests a cricket or football team; it is the alphabet's first eleven letters, A to K, from which every letter of the answer is drawn.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft or vehicle seized by force and diverted is said to have been commandeered illegally this way.

clue.text: Unyielding in charge, like the Screwtape Letters?

parts.note: iron as an adjective means firm and unbending, as in an iron will

explanation.surface: A stern, unbending person runs things, rather like the senior devil in C. S. Lewis's book.
explanation.walkthrough: The Screwtape Letters is C. S. Lewis's book of advice from a senior devil, which says the opposite of what it means.
explanation.definitionFit: The book's letters praise temptation so that readers take away the reverse message, which is the essence of saying one thing to mean another.

clue.text: Nymph's letter for the radio

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the mountain nymph of Greek myth who could only repeat others' words
second meaning: the code word for E in the NATO phonetic alphabet used in radio communication

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are the mythical nymph and the radio code word for E.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend the nymph pined for Narcissus, and radio operators use the same name in the phonetic alphabet for the fifth letter.

clue.text: Leaders in the Economist repeated, repeated within as paired discussions

indicators.note: leaders in means the first letters of the words that follow are taken, starting with the

parts.note: the leader of Economist, E, followed by the pair of leaders from the and Economist said a second time

indicators.note: within means the second copy of the doubled string goes inside the word as

parts.note: repeated again gives the doubled four-letter string once more

explanation.surface: Editorials in a magazine are run twice over as if they were face-to-face talks.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural is unusual but fair: several private talks are tête-à-têtes, and 'as' is split around the second copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A private conversation between two people is named from the French for head to head, and the plural covers several such talks.

clue.text: Hustle confused seeker of purloined letter, for example

definitions.text: seeker of purloined letter, for example

indicators.note: confused means the letters of hustle are jumbled into another order

explanation.surface: Someone hurrying in a muddle is looking for a stolen piece of post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Purloined Letter' is the Edgar Allan Poe story in which the detective Dupin recovers a stolen letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Poe's Dupin, who tracks down the stolen letter, is a detective, and this informal word means a detective.

clue.text: Like parts of eg UK, over time, for ruling class

indicators.note: over means the word for capitals sits over and around the abbreviation for time

parts.note: in 'eg UK' the letters U and K are capitals, so that part is in capital letters

explanation.surface: Parts of Britain, over the years, have served the interests of those in power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like parts of eg UK' is typographical: 'eg' is in small letters but 'UK' is in capitals. Put T inside UPPER CASE.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest hereditary social rank in a hierarchy holds power and privilege, the elite who rule.

clue.text: Open University letter, moving right to left, that gives better options

indicators.note: moving right to left means the R (right) is shifted from the end to the front

parts.note: OU is the abbreviation for the Open University, the UK distance-learning university
taken as written

explanation.surface: A university note, written from right to left, offers a choice of courses.
explanation.walkthrough: Take OULETTER and move its final R, the abbreviation for right, round to the far left.
explanation.definitionFit: The casino wheel offers a bettor (one who bets) many wagers: red, black, odd, even, single numbers.

clue.text: Submit page on Oscar in ordinary language

indicators.note: in means the letters for page and Oscar are placed inside the word for ordinary language

parts.note: prose is ordinary written language as opposed to verse

indicators.note: on means the letter for page comes upon, directly before, the letter for Oscar

parts.note: Oscar is the radio code word for O

explanation.surface: An author hands in a page about an Academy Award, written in plain language.
explanation.definitionFit: To put forward a plan or motion for consideration is to offer it up, as when one moves a resolution.

clue.text: Spell of work on island that makes capital

parts.note: a shift is a period of work
a key is a low island or reef, as in the Florida Keys

explanation.surface: A stint of labour on a small island earns someone money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests money, but here it is a capital letter.
explanation.definitionFit: On a keyboard, holding down this key produces an uppercase letter instead of the small one.

clue.text: Letters rewritten for newcomer

indicators.note: rewritten means the letters of letters are written out again in a new order

explanation.surface: Correspondence is redrafted for someone who has just arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who arrives to make a home in a new country or colony is a recent arrival there.

clue.text: Snarl from figure in world of magic not opening letter

indicators.note: not opening letter means the word is taken without its first letter

parts.note: a pentangle is a five-pointed star used as a magic symbol

explanation.surface: A magician's figure gets in a tangle when it is missing its first character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snarl' suggests a growl; here it is a verb meaning to tangle.
explanation.definitionFit: To snarl a rope or line is to twist it into a knotted mess, the same as making it tangled.

clue.text: Person overusing one vowel — so get it changed

indicators.note: changed means the letters of so, get and it are put into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone who repeats a vowel too often is told to do something about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The vowel is I: a self-centred person says 'I' too often.
explanation.definitionFit: A conceited, self-absorbed person keeps talking about himself, saying the first-person pronoun far too much.

clue.text: Our object, discarding hearts and starting with clubs, is trying to win hand

indicators.note: starting with means the letter for clubs goes at the front

parts.note: C is the card abbreviation for clubs
taken as written

indicators.note: discarding means the letter for hearts is dropped from the word for object

parts.note: a thing is an object
H is the card abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: A card player throws away hearts and leads clubs in an effort to take the trick.
explanation.walkthrough: The card-game picture misleads: the 'hand' sought is a hand in marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooing someone in the old sense means seeking their agreement to marry, asking for their hand.

clue.text: Dish included in some letters, as Americans serve it

indicators.note: included in means the answer sits inside the run of letters in some letters

explanation.surface: A food item turns up among the post, the way Americans would serve it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As Americans serve it' says the dish is spelt the American way, without the -TTE ending.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg preparation beaten and fried in a pan is a dish, spelt here in the US form.

clue.text: Ministerial assistant's uniform in box

indicators.note: in means the letter for uniform is placed inside the word for box

parts.note: a crate is a wooden packing box
Uniform is the radio code word for U

explanation.surface: A government minister's aide has his outfit packed away in a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ministerial' suggests politics, but this minister is a church one.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Church of England this is a junior cleric who helps the vicar or rector of a parish.

clue.text: They work on transforming characters, reforming credos

indicators.note: reforming means the letters of credos are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: Reformers rework beliefs as they try to change people's characters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' are letters, symbols turned into code.
explanation.definitionFit: People who write cipher or computer code convert text and symbols into another form.

clue.text: Dave, having misplaced vowels, said to be very upset

indicators.note: having misplaced vowels means the A and E in Dave swap their places

parts.note: stated means said

explanation.surface: A man named Dave, who has jumbled his vowels, is reported to be very distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the two vowels of the name trade places; its consonants stay where they are.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shattered or overwhelmed with grief or shock is utterly distraught.

clue.text: Letter's demand producing tear

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the payment a landlord, one who lets property, asks for
second meaning: a rip or split, as in cloth

explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' is not correspondence but one who lets property, a landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord charges periodic payment for property, and a rip in fabric has the same name.

clue.text: Are you followed by bee and why? It's said to make you red

indicators.note: said means the words are read as spoken letter names

parts.words: Are you followed by bee and why
parts.note: are you, bee and why, said in that order, sound like the letter names R, U, B and Y

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about four sounds that supposedly make a person blush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Are', 'you', 'bee' and 'why' sound like the letter names R, U, B, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The precious gemstone is a deep crimson, and its name is used for that shade of colour.

clue.text: Car model's sound — G, J, P or R, initially

definitions.text: G, J, P or R, initially

indicators.note: sound means the answer is pronounced the same as the name of the car

parts.note: the Beetle is the classic Volkswagen car model

explanation.surface: A car model's sound is spelt out by four letters given as initials.
explanation.walkthrough: G, J, P and R are the initials of George, John, Paul and Ringo.
explanation.definitionFit: George Harrison, John Lennon, Paul McCartney and Ringo Starr were the four members of the Liverpool band.

clue.text: It scores at least 14 in itself

definitions.text: It scores at least 14 in itself

parts.words: It scores at least 14 in itself
parts.note: the tile values of the board game's own name add up to fourteen, more with bonus squares

explanation.walkthrough: Using its tile values (S1 C3 R1 A1 B3 B3 L1 E1) the name scores 14, more on a premium square.
explanation.definitionFit: The board game in which players score points by placing lettered tiles is named here, and its name is itself a playable word.
